title: Research Methods in Psychology Adventure 1: Experimental Methods
welcome_lead: Today you'll compare lab, field, natural and quasi-experiments.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In a lab experiment, the researcher controls the setting and manipulates the IV (Loftus & Palmer 1974).

Pros: replicable, causal inference; Cons: low ecological validity, demand characteristics.

Field experiments manipulate the IV in a natural setting (Piliavin 1969 subway helping).

Higher ecological validity, but harder to control extraneous variables.

Natural experiments: the IV varies in nature — e.g. Rutter's Romanian orphans (institutional care vs adopted).

Quasi-experiments: the IV is a participant characteristic — age, sex, diagnosis. Random allocation impossible, so causal claims are weaker.

Strict cause-and-effect → lab.

Real-world generalisability → field.

Ethical impossibility of manipulation → natural or quasi.

Triangulation: combining methods strengthens conclusions.
